discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators
motivation: Topological insulators changed how we classify electronic matter. Kane (with Mele) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a Z2 topological phase, an insulating bulk with protected, spin-momentum-locked boundary states, and extended the classification to three dimensions. Molenkamp gave the first experimental proof, observing quantized edge conduction of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells in 2007. Hasan used angle-resolved and spin-resolved photoemission to directly image the surface Dirac cones and their helical spin texture in Bi-based compounds, establishing three-dimensional topological insulators as real materials. Together these discoveries, confirmed across many materials and probes, created a new paradigm linking band topology to measurable electronic structure. They underpin the later discoveries of Weyl semimetals, topological superconductivity and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and they redirected research in quantum materials worldwide.
